review: initial diagnosis only; later acceptance calls separate
scope: Frontmatter and Part I; all seven canonical Markdown files and all seven sidecars read fully, including equations, tables, captions, alt text and fold contents. Plan global and Part purposes/order read.
audience: Undergraduate calculus, basic linear algebra and ordinary expectation, variance, standard deviation and probability density. Neuroscience and specialized process/information tools must be taught.
method: Direct passage review; do not claim semantic acceptance from extraction or hashes. Parent coordinates any whole-guide concept-index tooling.

overall.chapter_order: Sound: signals/model -> persistence/neutral geometry -> projected diffusion -> long delay/boundaries/drift -> information bound -> readout. No chapter move justified.
overall.main_path_issue: Several definitions/results needed by later main text occur only in always-folded explanations, despite reading-guide lines 118 and 145 offering a first pass in which necessary explanations stay in main text.
overall.full_expanded_path: Most teaching is earlier when folds are opened. Remaining local repairs concern symbol roles and continuous-noise notation.

earliest_dependent_use.reason: The model replaces count fluctuations with sqrt(r_i)dB_i; reader must know what random increment dB_i is and its variance to interpret the replacement and units.

teaching.status: adequate Brownian process definition inside always-folded note, especially line142; does not explicitly bridge dB to B(t+dt)-B(t)
increment covariance appears later at dependent diffusion calculation

findings.minimal_repair: Keep a short Brownian definition/scale on main reading path before first stochastic equation. Explicitly connect dB_i to a Brownian increment with mean zero and variance dt; leave derivation in fold. This is not a request to teach general stochastic integration.

earliest_dependent_use.reason: Gaussian likelihood is converted to an equivalent observation model; later backward precision calculation combines likelihoods.

teaching.status: adequate likelihood and score teaching, but entirely inside always-folded derivation; definition at82

findings.minimal_repair: Make the short likelihood definition available in main text near Fisher information, with its distinction from a probability over angles. Retain log-likelihood/score algebra folded. A short reminder in readout may suffice if it supplies this meaning before the observation model.

findings.concept: Finite-time ideal readout result and coth

earliest_dependent_use.reason: The main text gives numerical finite-duration variance ratios that require the finite-time solution, and line330 later states a coth curve.

teaching.status: solution, finite-time formula and hyperbolic function definitions only inside always-folded mathematical solution

findings.minimal_repair: Keep finite-time result and compact function meaning on main path before numerical interpretation; fold only integration steps. Do not move the whole proof.

findings.concept: Continuous white-noise term in two-time-scale model

earliest_dependent_use.reason: xi_i is added to a time derivative. Earlier model used increments sqrt(r_i)dB_i, while xi_i is described only as zero-mean noise with 'same Poisson strength'. Without temporal covariance/increment meaning the reader cannot see what random process is specified or why diffusion remains sum a_i^2 r_i at298.

teaching.status: increment form for noise; no corresponding definition of white-noise derivative xi_i
strength and placement are mentioned, but bridge between xi_i dt and Brownian increments absent

findings.minimal_repair: Introduce xi_i as idealized white noise through its increment meaning or write this equation using the already-taught increment form. State independence and local variance scale at the same point. No extra white-noise calculus chapter needed.

earliest_dependent_use.reason: The text says the count is split, then introduces dM_i without explicitly equating it to count minus conditional mean.

teaching.status: role is strongly implied by split and moment conditions; short explicit definition would remove inference

findings.minimal_repair: Give dM_i=dN_i-r_i dt before or in the split. This is a local symbol-role repair, not a missing probability prerequisite.

optional_role_repairs.assessment: Algebra defines F_i adequately; useful short lead-in would call it mean activation change per time.

Definitions are mathematically available within the matrix equation. Useful plain lead-in: K gives first-order return/feedback response acting on activation disturbances; R collects local spike increment variance strengths. Do not label this missing standard linear algebra.
Existing purpose appears just after equations. Moving that purpose sentence before equations helps the reader know why v is introduced; retain normalization explanation after.

false_positives_resolved.item: Frontmatter paper results, appendix map and Part introductions
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Previews with plain descriptions and future links; no dependent calculation requires full Fisher information, filtering, random-field or matrix proofs here.

false_positives_resolved.item: Poisson process first appears before its binomial-limit derivation
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Distribution, count/rate meanings and mean/variance are explicitly supplied before examples. Proof may remain folded; ordinary expectation and variance are assumed.

false_positives_resolved.item: Dirac delta follows first spike equation by one paragraph
false_positives_resolved.resolution: The equation is immediately unpacked into pulse, time constant and one-unit activation jump before reasoning continues. No displaced teaching or glossary dependence.

Plain definitions in Ch1 main text at278 precede their later use. Formal formula folded but Ch6 supplies Brownian covariance formula and shared-increment explanation at74-80 before integrating; no need to move full Ch2 covariance derivation.
Definitions in Persistence57-59 precede two-cell disturbance reasoning and the later linearized model.
Ch3 derives tangent and zero-eigenvector meaning before projecting noise; no prerequisite for a full abstract eigentheory lesson beyond assumed linear algebra.

false_positives_resolved.item: Multidimensional diffusion tensor appears in equation before name
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Coordinate tangents, dual normalization and same covariance calculation define entries at196-200; meaning is then unpacked at211. A short lead-in is possible but no substantial concept-order gap.

Main text defines local distinguishability, explains sensitivity vs noise with a count example and gives single/population formulas before Cramer Rao use. Score proof can stay folded except its likelihood definition is needed later.

false_positives_resolved.item: Cramer Rao and Cauchy Schwarz proofs folded
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Main text supplies estimator, unbiasedness, smoothness scope and bound before use; undergraduate linear algebra plus immediate dot-product explanation supports following information-diffusion proof.

false_positives_resolved.item: Mutual excitation and inhibition transfer rule
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Ch3 defines phi(g)=g/tau on positive range before Ch4 says same linear rule; coordinate and positive-domain restrictions are explicit.
Beginning-of-increment vs midpoint conventions are taught in Ch4 main text before convention-dependent drift interpretation; details may stay folded.

false_positives_resolved.item: tau_m has prior torque meaning in folded eye mechanics
false_positives_resolved.resolution: Readout explicitly redefines it as response time; different chapter/domain and units prevent an order gap.

Line330 states duration is rescaled by L*, from which z=L/L* follows; sidecar alt explicitly writes z=L sqrt(2DJ). A local explicit equality could help but not a separate substantial prerequisite gap.
